topic: Coloprice Top: largest operators by published MW

facts: Catalogue: 2295 operators, 6116 facilities in 184 countries (as of 2026-11-04)
Largest by published MW — #1 Meta Platforms: 3 tracked facilities in 2 countries, 6,000 MW published (2 of 3 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #2 STACK Infrastructure: 49 tracked facilities in 11 countries, 5,673 MW published (48 of 49 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #3 Vantage Data Centers: 42 tracked facilities in 14 countries, 5,544 MW published (39 of 42 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #4 IREN: 9 tracked facilities in 3 countries, 5,460 MW published (8 of 9 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #5 CDC Data Centres: 19 tracked facilities in 2 countries, 3,308 MW published (13 of 19 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #6 OpenAI (developer Octans GA LLC): 1 tracked facilities in 1 country, 3,210 MW published (1 of 1 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #7 Crusoe: 4 tracked facilities in 1 country, 3,100 MW published (3 of 4 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #8 Nebius: 4 tracked facilities in 2 countries, 3,010 MW published (4 of 4 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #9 Aligned Data Centers: 40 tracked facilities in 5 countries, 2,935 MW published (16 of 40 sites publish MW)
Largest by published MW — #10 Google: 20 tracked facilities in 2 countries, 2,700 MW published (1 of 20 sites publish MW)

caption:
6,000 MW: Meta Platforms leads the Coloprice ranking of operators by published capacity.

STACK Infrastructure (5,673 MW) and Vantage Data Centers (5,544 MW) follow, then IREN with 5,460 MW. Meta gets there with 3 tracked facilities; STACK needs 49.

The ranking only counts MW that operators publish: Google shows 2,700 MW, but only 1 of its 20 sites discloses capacity. Largest by published MW, not an endorsement.

Data: Coloprice operator rankings, 4 Nov 2026. Sources on the last slide.

Should published MW be the yardstick for operators, or only energised capacity? Full ranking: link in bio.
